text:
maya: Heads up — nightly evals for pset29 show a weird spike in failures after the promptset v29 push to canary yesterday evening. the diff looks small but quality dropped on generative tests.

aj: ugh, example?

maya: pasted a couple below. note the extra emoji tokens popping into answers for explicit 'no' cases. seems like tokenization/escape handling changed in a few templates.

maya: sample 1 input: 'Is the following safe? — No'
maya: expected: 'No, it is not safe.'
maya: model output: 'No 😊, it is not safe.'

rachel: whoa. emoji insertion? that smells like a prompt formatting change adding a trailing unicode char or weird whitespace. did the pset tooling add an emoji in any templates?

samir: i grep'd the v29 promptpack, found this line in qgen template: 

```
Answer: {answer} 
Context: {ctx} 
Tone: friendly 🙂
```

samir: looks like someone added a tone hint with an emoji. that would change tokenization and could trigger generation bias.

leon: that would also change the token-level prefixes the model sees. with quantized kernels or shorter sequence fast paths, it can nudge logits.

aj: eval-bot, can you share the metric deltas for the affected buckets?

eval-bot: nightly-eval summary for pset29 v29 canary vs v28 baseline: overall pass rate down 6.8%, negation-specific F1 down 14%, generation neutral->emoji increase +3.4% absolute. 42 failing examples triaged as likely template-induced.

rachel: ok that points to the template change. we should either revert the emoji in promptpack or add a normalization step in prompt rendering to strip emoticons for sensitive tests.

maya: i'm going to file a patch to remove the emoji and kick a canary re-eval. canary id: canary-8912.

deploy-bot: deploy queued by maya for canary-8912 — promptpack v29-emoji-strip patch. CI lint ok.

aj: quick thought — instead of removing tone entirely, we could move tone hints to metadata that the model doesn't see in generation input (console-only). that keeps UX but not in-eval artifacts. file an RFC?

samir: agree. short-term revert to preserve quality, long-term move tone hints out of the final rendered prompt.

leon: also flag for quantization tests: this effect was amplified on the 4-bit quantized snapshots. we should add a regression test that pins tokenized prefix distributions across promptset changes.

maya: noted. i'll open two follow-ups: 1) revert patch + run re-eval (in-progress), 2) tracker for tooling change so tone hints live in metadata.

rachel: thanks. if canary re-eval looks green, we can rebaseline once we have the RFC for metadata approach. :thumbsup:

aj: tagging ops to watch canary: @deploy-bot please alert if latency or error rates spike after the tweak.

deploy-bot: will monitor canary-8912 for 60m and report back.

maya: quick note for posterity — watch out for non-ascii UX changes in promptpacks, even small emoji additions can create outsized quality shifts.

samir: agreed. adding to promptpack contribution guide checklist: verify no inline emoji in rendered prompts for eval suites.

leon: cool, marking this resolved for now pending re-eval.

maya: thanks all.
